chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyah (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: My uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim narrated to me, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Barqi, from his father Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, who linked it up to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him),
He said: The people are two: a scholar and a learner; and the rest of the people are 'Hamaj' (the unrefined/ignorant), and the 'Hamaj' are in the Fire.

key_terms.هَمَجٌ: The unrefined, ignorant, or common masses

ai.seo_question: What are the two main categories of people according to this hadith from al-Khisal?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq highlights the dichotomy between the learned and the seekers, categorizing the rest of humanity as 'Hamaj' (the unrefined masses) destined for the Fire. This classification underscores the Shia emphasis on *'Ilm* (knowledge) as the primary criterion for spiritual distinction, contrasting the conscious pursuit of divine truth with the passive ignorance of the general populace.
